title: SqlProof scenario (version 1)
description: A named, seeded database state: pinned rows plus generated filler. See https://sqlproof.com/guides/scenarios/.

seed.description: Every generated value is a function of this seed.

clock.description: ISO 8601 timestamp that now()-style column defaults become. Defaults to 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z; no timezone means UTC.

tables.description: Table name (bare or schema-qualified) to its row groups, laid out in order.

^x-.description: Extensions for tools building on scenarios; not part of the scenario.

oneOf.description: n rows with the columns in `set` pinned; every other column is generated.
n rows with the columns in `set` pinned. Unlike a cohort, a fill grows in a scale sweep, so pin per-row values with the value generators (format, one_of, some_of, pick).
One row other rows can reference as {ref: <name>}.
Size this table by its parents. Cannot be combined with other groups in phase 1.

where.description: Parents whose cohorts pin these values, a named row, or null for every parent.

default.description: Children per other parent. Defaults to 0.

column.description: The foreign-key column, when there is more than one into the parent.

value.description: A literal Postgres can read, a reference to a named row, a value generator, a list (an array column; its elements may be format generators) or an object (a json column). An object that is exactly {ref: <name>} is always a reference. An object with a format, one_of, some_of, pick or json key is a generator, so a json value of that shape is written {json: <value>}.

data.description: A scalar, array or json object that cannot read as a generator.

format.description: Text with {n} replaced by each row's number in its table (1, 2, 3, ...).

generator.description: A value that differs per row: a pure function of the scenario, its seed, the column and the row.

oneOf.description: One of the values per row.
An array of count distinct values from the list, for an array column.

Values another column of the scenario holds (table.column): an array of count distinct ones for an array column, or one value without count. The source must be a column the scenario computes per row: a literal, a generator, a key or a UNIQUE column.
A json value written so it cannot read as a generator.
